speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your appointment. I see you are experiencing neck and arm pain along with paresthesias and muscle weakness. To understand the underlying cause, can you tell me how long these symptoms have been present and if they radiate in a specific pattern down your arm?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The patient reports a year-long history of burning neck and arm pain with paresthesias, worsening hand weakness over the last 3 months. Given your history of diabetes and hypertension, have you noticed any numbness in the soles of your feet or changes in your vision or urination patterns?

REQUEST TEST: Fasting_Blood_Glucose, HbA1c, BMP

speaker: Doctor
text: The test results for your blood sugar and basic metabolic panel are normal, which helps rule out acute diabetic complications. However, given your history of hypertension and a prior motor vehicle accident, could you describe if your neck pain is worse with turning your head or lifting your arms, and do you have any headaches or difficulty walking?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) with possible cervical spondylotic myelopathy.

The presence of fasciculations combined with absent reflexes, muscle weakness, and burning pain in a patient with normal blood sugar strongly suggests a motor neuron disease like ALS. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Cervical Spine.
